findings.summary: subtotal() iterates range(len(items)-1), silently dropping the last line item from the sum.
findings.failure_scenario: Given items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop runs only for i=0 and returns 100 instead of 300. For a single-item invoice items=[{"price":100,"qty":1}], range(0) is empty and it returns 0. The docstring says "Sum price*qty across line items"; there is no summary/total row convention in the data model, so real line items are omitted.

findings.summary: mean_line_value() divides a subtotal that excludes the last item by the full item count, and raises ZeroDivisionError on empty lists.
findings.failure_scenario: subtotal() sums only n-1 items but division is by len(items)=n, so the mean is systematically too low (e.g. two items of 100 and 200 give subtotal 100, 100//2=50 instead of 150). For items=[] it evaluates subtotal([])//0 and raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: allocate_tax() rounds each share independently, so the allocated amounts do not sum back to tax_cents.
findings.failure_scenario: With tax_cents=100 and weights=[1,1,1], each share is round(100/3)=round(33.33)=33, summing to 99 (one cent lost). With tax_cents=10 and weights=[1,1], round(5)=5,5 sums to 10 fine, but tax_cents=100, weights=[1,1] each round(50)=50 ok; however weights=[1,1,1,1,1,1] with tax=100 gives round(16.67)=17 each = 102, over-allocating. The docstring claims allocations sum to the original tax; they do not. Additionally, empty weights or all-zero weights make total=0, causing ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: late_fee() does not guard against negative days_late, producing a negative (credit) fee.
findings.failure_scenario: If days_late is negative (e.g. an order paid early, days_late=-3), late_fee returns -1500, applying a credit instead of zero fee. There is no max(0, ...) clamp.

findings.summary: subtotal iterates range(len(items)-1), silently dropping the last line item from the sum.
findings.failure_scenario: For items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop only covers index 0, returning 100 instead of 300. The docstring says "sum across line items"; the last item is always omitted. There is no "summary/total row" convention in the data—this off-by-one under-counts every invoice.

findings.summary: mean_line_value divides a subtotal that excludes the last item by the full item count, producing a wrong average.
findings.failure_scenario: For items with 2 lines of value 100 and 200, subtotal returns 100 (last item dropped) and len(items)=2, so mean is 50 instead of the correct 150. The numerator and denominator disagree on how many items are counted.

findings.summary: mean_line_value raises ZeroDivisionError on an empty items list.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling mean_line_value([]) computes subtotal([])//len([]) = 0//0, raising ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0 or handling the empty case.

findings.summary: allocate_tax rounds each share independently, so the allocated cents do not sum back to tax_cents.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(10, [1,1,1]): each share = round(10/3) = round(3.333) = 3, sum = 9, losing 1 cent versus the 10-cent tax. Conversely round-up cases can over-allocate. The claimed invariant that the split sums to the original tax is violated.

findings.summary: allocate_tax divides by sum(weights) with no guard, raising ZeroDivisionError for empty or all-zero weights.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, []) or allocate_tax(100, [0,0]) makes total=0, and tax_cents*w/total raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning an empty/zero allocation.

findings.summary: late_fee does not clamp negative days_late, producing a negative (credit) fee.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, i.e. a negative late fee, when a not-yet-late order should yield 0.

findings.summary: subtotal() iterates range(len(items)-1), silently dropping the last line item from the sum.
findings.failure_scenario: For items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}] subtotal returns 100 instead of 300; the last item is always excluded. The docstring says "Sum price*qty across line items" — real invoice lists are actual line items, not summary rows, so every subtotal is understated by the last line. For a single-item invoice it returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value() divides an already-truncated subtotal (missing the last item) by the full item count, and divides by zero for empty lists.
findings.failure_scenario: Because subtotal() omits the last item but len(items) counts all items, the mean is wrong on two axes: for items=[{price:100,qty:1},{price:200,qty:1}] it returns 100//2=50 rather than 150. For items=[] it raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: allocate_tax() rounds each share independently, so the allocations do not necessarily sum back to tax_cents (and total==0 raises ZeroDivisionError).
findings.failure_scenario: For tax_cents=100, weights=[1,1,1]: each share is round(33.33)=33, summing to 99, losing a cent — contradicting the stated goal that allocations sum back to the original tax. With weights that round up, the sum can exceed tax_cents (e.g. tax_cents=10, weights=[1,1,1] gives 3+3+3=9; other distributions overshoot). Also weights=[] or all-zero weights raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: late_fee() does not guard against negative days_late, producing a negative (credit) fee.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, applying a credit instead of no fee when a caller passes a not-yet-late (negative) day count.
